image_description: A low-angle shot of a large, ornate Baroque-style pipe organ installed in a church or cathedral. The instrument features a massive wooden case with intricate carvings and gilding. Multiple tiers of vertical metal pipes (likely tin or lead alloy) are visible, arranged symmetrically with varying heights creating a stepped silhouette. The central section has taller pipes, flanked by shorter ones. The ceiling above is white with decorative plasterwork. No console, keyboards, or pedalboard are visible in this specific framing, which focuses on the upper facade and pipe array.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific taxonomic classification of the instrument and distinguish it from other large architectural structures.
To verify the 3D spatial relationship between the pipes and the wooden case, ensuring no 'melting' or depth collapse common in AI generations of complex repetitive structures.
To check for boundary bleeding between individual pipes and the background/case, ensuring each pipe is a distinct, solid object.
To assess the realism of the complex textures in the carved wood and metallic pipes, looking for smearing or unnatural patterns.

focus_areas: Symmetry and alignment of vertical pipes
Texture consistency of metallic pipes vs. carved wood
Structural integrity of the ornate wooden case
Edge sharpness between pipes and background
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the regularity of the pipes. AI often struggles with repeating vertical elements, causing slight warping or inconsistent spacing. Check if the reflections on the metal pipes are consistent with a single light source. Verify that the ornate wood carvings do not dissolve into noise or mushy textures upon close inspection.
